prompt:
Research what the SQLite project officially documents about the maximum database size and maximum row size. Cite the official SQLite limits page and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the official documented limits from the SQLite project regarding maximum database size and maximum row size, as specified on their official limits page.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "Maximum Database Size The maximum size of an SQLite database is about 281 terabytes." | CLAIM: The official maximum size limit for an SQLite database.
SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The maximum size of a row in an SQLite table is defined by the size of the page." | CLAIM: The rule that determines the maximum size of a row in SQLite.
SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The theoretical maximum size of a row in an SQLite database is about 1.3 gigabytes." | CLAIM: The theoretical maximum size limit for a single row in an SQLite database.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A hard upper byte limit for a row implemented independently from the database page size configuration.
